name_en: Carleson's theorem on almost-everywhere Fourier convergence
literal_source_claim: The Fourier series of an L^2 function converges almost everywhere.
canonical_claim: For every complex-valued square-integrable function on the one-dimensional circle, its symmetric Fourier partial sums converge to the function almost everywhere.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: complex-valued measurable functions on AddCircle T, normally T = 2*pi or an equivalent unit-circle normalization, modulo almost-everywhere equality in Lp C 2 haarAddCircle.
quantifiers: for every square-integrable complex-valued function f on the circle
as the symmetric cutoff N tends to infinity
hypotheses: f is measurable and square-integrable with respect to normalized Haar measure
conclusion: The symmetric partial sums sum_{|n| <= N} fourierCoeff f n * fourier n x tend to a representative of f at almost every x.
excluded_degenerate_cases: Normalization of the circle and Haar measure, use of Lp classes versus representatives, the value at null-set points, complex versus real codomain, and symmetric versus one-sided enumeration remain statement-phase decisions. T = 0 is excluded by the positive-period AddCircle interface.
